indigo-ink.purpose: The only accent. Links, active nav trail, focus rings, graph root node, selection at 20%, blockquote rule at 45%. Never a decorative fill.

indigo-wash.purpose: The accent diluted to a hover/active surface tint, paired with Indigo Wash Ink for text sitting on it.

warm-paper.purpose: The page ground. Deliberately not white — the hue-85 warmth is the 'paper' half of the north star.

paper-card.purpose: Pure white, one step above the page. A card being whiter than the ground is the inversion that replaces a shadow.

paper-tint.purpose: Secondary/muted surface: input wells, inactive chips, the search trigger field.

sidebar-paper.purpose: The navigation rail, one tonal step off the page so it reads as a different material without a heavier border.

ink-muted.purpose: Secondary text, captions, default icon color, h4, blockquote body.

rule.purpose: Every border and input stroke in the system. One value, one weight, no exceptions.

panel-note.purpose: Callout: note. Drives the left rule, the masked glyph and the switcher dot.

panel-tip.purpose: Callout: tip. Also the resolved-thread highlight wash at 16%.

panel-important.purpose: Callout: important. Also the AI-authorship avatar fill.

panel-warning.purpose: Callout: warning. Also the open-thread highlight wash at 26% with a 55% inset underline.

pin-open.purpose: Comment pin fill while a thread is open. Theme-independent by design — it ships with its own ink.

pin-done.purpose: Comment pin fill once a thread is resolved. Theme-independent, paired with its own ink.

draw-ink.purpose: Default stroke and label color for drawn diagrams; the ramp's five hues (blue, green, amber, red, violet) accompany it and lift wholesale in dark mode.

display.purpose: Page and document h1. Sora 700 with -0.015em tracking.

headline.purpose: Document h2, with a hairline rule beneath — the only decorative line in prose.

body.purpose: All prose at 1.7 line-height, capped at a 46rem measure.

label.purpose: Chips, metadata, rail previews, kbd hints.

code.purpose: Inline code on an 8% current-color wash; blocks on a 5% foreground-over-card panel with a rule.

shadows.name: seated
shadows.purpose: Form controls only — inputs and select triggers. Keeps a transparent well from dissolving into the page.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Cards that carry their own content region. The hairline does the real work.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, sheets, the mobile drawer. Long, soft, heavily negative-spread — something well above the page, not merely lifted. 60% black in dark mode.

motion.name: pane-ease
motion.purpose: The sidebar navigation stack's push/pop. The session's one authored movement.

motion.name: pane-duration
motion.purpose: Identical in both directions — a faster return reads as a mismatch, not as intent.

motion.name: pane-relight
motion.purpose: The returning parent's opacity recovers over the first 110ms of a pop, so no grey band drags behind the departing pane.

motion.name: stage
motion.purpose: Dialog stage changes (form to creating to follow-up). Deliberately quieter than the panes.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Annotation highlight background, graph node border, hover tints.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every motion branches here. The change still has to be perceptible — a crossfade, never a jump cut.

narrative.overview:
The phrase is not aspirational — it is already written at the top of style.css, and the system has been obeying it. The ground is paper that was never bleached white (a warm near-white at hue 85 degrees), the type is ink pressed into it, and exactly one cool indigo is allowed to glow: on links, on the active trail, on a focus ring, on the root node of a graph. Everything that glows is structure. Nothing glows because it wanted attention.

The register is quiet, precise and unhurried at the level of the page, and instrument-grade at the level of the control. Those are not in tension: the page recedes so that a passage of prose is the loudest thing on screen, while every control that frames it — a 36px button, a 6px status dot, a hairline rule under an h2, a comment pin sized in rem so it stays legible in any prose — is exact, compact and unambiguous. This is a surface people read for an hour and then annotate in the margin. Chrome that competes with the text is a defect, and a control that leaves you guessing its state is also a defect.

Depth is nearly absent by design. Surfaces separate by hairline border and tonal shift, not by shadow; a shadow means the element has genuinely left the page. Color is rationed the same way: five semantic panel hues and six diagram hues exist, and emerald/amber/red are spoken for by the indexing lifecycle and may not be borrowed. Confirmed anti-references: the generic AI-SaaS gradient deck, enterprise wiki beige, and the Notion clone.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, indigo ink, one accent that only ever marks structure.
Flat by default; hairline borders and tonal steps carry all separation.
One stylesheet serves both reading and writing — they are pixel-identical.
Status is a 6px dot, not a banner.
Every color token is declared twice, light and dark, with no exceptions.
Identity is derived, never uploaded: initials on a hue hashed from the user id.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every color token is declared twice — once in :root, once in .dark. A token that exists in only one theme is a bug, not a light-mode optimization. The two exceptions are deliberate: the comment pin's fill and ink travel as a fixed pair, because a pin whose ink follows the theme while its fill does not is unreadable in one of the two.

rules.name: The One Indigo Rule
rules.body: The accent marks structure and nothing else — link, active trail, focus, selection, graph root. It is never a background for a hero, a card, or a section. Its rarity is what makes the active row findable.

rules.name: The Reserved Signal Rule
rules.body: Emerald, amber and red belong to the indexing lifecycle. Do not borrow them for emphasis, decoration, or a second meaning of 'good'. If a new state needs a color, take it from the panel ramp.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: Reading and writing share a single stylesheet. A panel, a table, a diagram or a code block must be pixel-identical whether the page is being read or edited. Any type rule that applies to only one of the two is a bug.

rules.name: The Display-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: Sora is for headings and diagram labels. It never sets body copy, button text, or UI labels.

rules.name: The Loaded-Weight Rule
rules.body: Only the weights actually requested from the font provider may be specified. The stylesheet currently asks for 650 and 620 while loading 600 and 700, so those headings silently snap to a neighbour — either widen the font request or move to the loaded steps.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds 46rem. Anything that wants the full column — a revision table, a diff, a graph — is not prose and belongs in a rail widget or a maximized dialog.

rules.name: The Two Modes Rule
rules.body: A route is either a document (the content column grows, main scrolls, chrome padding applies) or a fill surface (the route owns the viewport and scrolls something inside itself). Never both.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow means the element is floating above the document — a dialog, a popover, a dropdown, a drawer. If it scrolls with the page, it gets a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders are 1px, one color token, everywhere. Weight is never used for emphasis; if a boundary needs to be stronger, change the tone on either side of it.

rules.name: The Round Means Count Rule
rules.body: Fully-round shapes are reserved for things that represent a quantity or an identity — badges, avatars, comment pins, status dots. Controls are never pill-shaped.

rules.name: The Pin Carries Its Own Ink Rule
rules.body: The comment pin's fill and ink are a fixed pair, theme-independent. Anything that sits on a tinted highlight rather than on the page must carry both halves of its contrast.

rules.name: The Derived Identity Rule
rules.body: There is no avatar storage. Identity marks are computed from the user id, and machine authorship is always visually distinct from human authorship.

dos: Do keep the accent for structure — link, active trail, focus ring, graph root, selection. If a new element wants Indigo Ink, ask what structure it marks.
Do declare every new color token in both :root and .dark, in the same order, in the same file.
Do separate surfaces with the 1px rule token and a tonal step. Reach for a shadow only when the element genuinely floats.
Do express prose in the shared stylesheet so the reader and the editor stay pixel-identical.
Do cap prose at the 46rem measure and put anything wider in a rail widget or a maximized dialog.
Do pair every motion with a prefers-reduced-motion branch that keeps the change perceptible — a 120ms crossfade, not a jump cut.
Do give focus a 3px ring plus a border shift, and drive validity from aria-invalid rather than a class.
Do size annotation affordances in rem so they survive whatever prose scale they land in.
donts: Don't introduce a gradient background, a glassmorphic card, or a glowing orb. The AI is a capability here, not a look.
Don't borrow emerald, amber or red for emphasis — they are the indexing lifecycle's, and a second meaning makes the dot unreadable.
Don't add a resting shadow to anything that scrolls with the page.
Don't set body copy, buttons or UI labels in Sora.
Don't specify a font weight the stylesheet does not actually load.
Don't animate anything at rest except the amber indexing pulse; that motion is information, and a second moving thing dilutes it.
Don't use a fully-round radius on a control. Round means a count or an identity.
Don't put a status, count or relation behind a tab when a collapsed rail row could show it.
Don't let a machine-authored item render with a person's initials.
Don't reach for md:, xl: or 2xl: for new layout work; this shell hinges at lg and reflows content at sm.
